title: Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (III: AthleanX, Kinobody, Scott Herman...)
summary: Part 3 of NH's channel grading series: 20 criteria scored 0-10 (programming, experience, integrity, usefulness, character, dogmatism, originality, blackpill, humor, parasocial, empathy, god complex, production, science, clickbait, recycling, conciseness, seniority, supplements, physique). Totals: Scott Herman 144.5, Natural Hypertrophy 143 (self-graded in a mocking 'cyborg' persona), Team3DAlpha 134, Steve Shaw 130, Kinobody 116, AthleanX 104.
claims: Steve Shaw scores 130: credited with bringing programming (reviews of German volume training, HIT) to YouTube lifters; programming 9, experience 9
Steve Shaw is very dogmatic (2.5), a trait typical of strength coaches that makes good strength teachers but closed minds
Natural-bodybuilding-is-a-joke content (Steve Shaw's most viewed video) blackpills viewers and paradoxically turns them into PED advocates
Working for Tiger Fitness, a garbage supplement company, costs Steve Shaw integrity and supplement points
Kinobody scores 116: knows programming (7.5) despite corny program names, but his experience is a narrow niche and his boxing advice is terrible
Kinobody's obsession with staying shredded creates small lifters and body dysmorphia; any big, strong natural must carry some fat at some point
Greg O'Gallagher does not understand body fat percentage and grossly underestimates his own (claims around 6%)
Kinobody has perfect production quality (drones, pro crews) but low empathy and fake-feeling persona
NH grades himself 143: programming 8.5 but says his strength methods don't work, integrity 9.5, originality 10, blackpill 9, supplements 10 for being anti-supplement
NH mocks his own channel: production quality 2, conciseness 2, videos too long, content branching away from lifting into philosophy and anime
Nobody gets 10 for experience before 10 years of serious hardcore training; NH has lifted around 15 years
Telling everyone they can achieve anything is an insult to people who lack what it takes
Scott Herman scores 144.5: integrity 9.5, character 10, very humble, but a physique that has not changed in about five years and heavy recycled clickbait
If your physique stops evolving, your knowledge stops evolving too
Generalist channels are more useful; someone subscribed only to NH would miss a lot
Scott Herman's 'don't do this' style clickbait and red-arrow thumbnails come from the AthleanX playbook and insult viewers' intelligence
Scott Herman never launching a supplement line despite millions of subscribers earns a 9, docked once for hyping BCAAs
Team3DAlpha scores 134: highly original (9.5) and drama-free, but programming hyper-focused on nucleus overload and videos built on single new studies (science 3)
Using enhanced bodybuilders as examples for naturals is a form of blackpill even when the advice is good
Supplements like ecdysterone and turkesterone have never created high-level physiques
AthleanX scores 104: integrity 0 over the fake weights fiasco and banning critics, programming 3.5, yet production 10 and originality 10 as the original physio-style channel
AthleanX is newbie land: its advice keeps people small so the channel retains an endless supply of beginners
Anyone who thinks AthleanX is a good source of information is not someone to take advice from
AthleanX made 'science-based' titles a clickbait tool (science 2) and invented fitness clickbait thumbnails (clickbait 1)
NH doubts Jeff Cavaliere's claimed 200 lb at 5'6 and estimates 150-160 lb
Big creators who profit from their own supplement lines are graded down for it
